subject: Investigate: self-serve credit anomalies for ClearLeaf Health (possible abuse)
messages:
From: Nicole Ayres <nicole.ayres@clearleafhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: security@clearleafhealth.com
Date: 2027-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unusual distribution of self-serve credits across our org

Hi Stephanie,

Hope youre well. We noticed something odd in our billing/credits report and wanted to surface it before we run a broader audit. Over the past 10 days, several ClearLeaf employees received self-serve trial grants from Redwood that look inconsistent with our internal onboarding (some appear to be multiple grants to generic or disposable accounts).

A couple of examples:
- sam+research@clearleafhealth.com (received 10,000 token credit)
- integrator01@clearleaftesting.mailinator.com (received 5,000 token credit)
- dev.clearleaf+trial@gmail.com (received 7,500 token credit)

Were concerned these might be test signups, automated scripts, or abuse that distorts our usage. Can you confirm whether Redwood has flags for duplicate accounts or device-level signals? If helpful, we can share the list of internal emails we want to consolidate under our org account.

Thanks for looking into this quickly — were preparing for a security review next week and would like a short summary we can include.

Best,
Nicole Ayres
Senior IT Risk Manager
ClearLeaf Health
security@clearleafhealth.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

I attached a quick export Nicole sent (signup_report.csv) and I captured a short list of suspicious domains (suspicious-domains.pdf).

Steph

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-16T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unusual distribution of self-serve credits across our org

Quick triage results (30-day window):

Summary:
- Total ClearLeaf-related signups: 42
- Flagged as high-confidence abuse: 8 accounts (matching pattern A)
- Medium-confidence: 4 accounts (pattern B)
- Likely legitimate: 30 accounts (company MX or SSO-associated)

Signals used (aggregate):
- Device fingerprint collision: 6+ accounts share identical UA string + canvas hash + first-kv-cache id.
- IP/ASN similarity: flagged accounts originate from 3 distinct datacenter ASNs with rotating IPs (likely proxy/VPN).
- Disposable domains: we matched ~12 emails to known disposable-as-a-service patterns (e.g., mailinator, tempmail, quickmail.*).
- Rapid create/use: 4 accounts created at < 2 minutes apart and consumed credits immediately.

Attachments: I exported the candidate list into signup_report.csv and a short snapshot of domain patterns into suspicious-domains.pdf.

Recommendation (ops + sales):
1) Immediately place a temporary "issue_hold" on further autonomous self-serve grants for any email matching company domain "clearleafhealth.com" when the signup pattern includes a disposable-domain forwarding address or device-fingerprint collision.
2) Roll back credits on high-confidence accounts (8) and flag for manual review. Provide sanitized list to the account team so they can coordinate outreach.
3) Do not mass-revoke medium-confidence accounts yet; instead flag them as "pending_verification" and ask customer for confirmation.

I can run an automated rollback script once sales signs off on the high-confidence list.

--
Dev Patel
Risk & Abuse Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-16T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unusual distribution of self-serve credits across our org

Thanks Dev — good work on the triage. From a customer-success/sales motion perspective Id prefer a two-step, conservative approach:

1) Customer-facing transparency: tell Nicole we found anomalies, and that were pausing further automatic trial grants for the ClearLeaf domain while we verify. Offer to consolidate valid accounts under one org seat if they provide a list or enable SSO.
2) Targeted rollback: proceed with revoking credits only for the 8 high-confidence accounts. We should include a brief explanation and next steps in the revocation notice (how to request restoration if the account owner believes its legitimate).
3) Medium-confidence accounts: hold in a pending state for 5 business days; if customer confirms, restore. If no confirmation, escalate to manual review.

I can draft the customer email for Nicole once Dev shares the sanitized list (no PII beyond the email addresses). Suggest timing: send the external notice after we complete the rollback, so we can report concrete remediation.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Nicole Ayres <nicole.ayres@clearleafhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-18T14:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual distribution of self-serve credits across our org

Hi Nicole,

Thanks again for flagging this — we completed a preliminary investigation and wanted to share what weve done and the next steps.

What we found:
- A small cluster of accounts (8) tied to ClearLeaf signups matched high-confidence abuse signals: disposable/forwarding addresses, device-fingerprint collisions, and proxy IP ASNs.
- An additional 4 accounts were medium-confidence and are being held pending verification.
- The remaining signups appear to be legitimate ClearLeaf employees (SSO or company MX).

Actions we took (completed):
- Reversed issued trial credits for the 8 high-confidence accounts and suspended their ability to request new grants.
- Placed a temporary hold on autonomous self-serve credit issuance for the clearleafhealth.com domain while we complete verification.
- Created an ops ticket for manual review of the 4 medium-confidence accounts (TKT-9245). Link: https://ops.redwood.com/tickets/TKT-9245

What we need from you (suggested, not required):
1) If you can, share a canonical list of ClearLeaf emails that should retain access (or enable SSO for the org). We will consolidate credits under a company-managed seat where possible.
2) If any of the reversed accounts are legitimate and you want credits restored, reply with the account owner and a short justification and well fast-track a restoration within 24 hours.

We aimed to minimize disruption — we only reversed credits for accounts with high-confidence signals. If youd like, Marissa can set up a 20-minute call to walk through the sanitized list and the verification workflow.

Apologies for the noise and thanks for your partnership on this.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0136
